questions.question: Who is the current Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of 2024)?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra was appointed as the Governor of RBI in December 2024, succeeding Shaktikanta Das.

questions.question: What does CRR stand for?
questions.explanation: CRR stands for Cash Reserve Ratio — the percentage of deposits banks must keep as cash with RBI.

questions.question: The headquarters of Reserve Bank of India is located in:
questions.explanation: The RBI headquarters is located in Mumbai (previously established in Kolkata in 1935, shifted to Mumbai in 1937).

questions.question: What is the full form of NEFT?
questions.explanation: NEFT stands for National Electronic Funds Transfer — a nation-wide payment system facilitating one-to-one funds transfer.

questions.question: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the minimum percentage of deposits that commercial banks must maintain in the form of:
questions.explanation: SLR is maintained in liquid assets: cash, gold, and government securities.

questions.question: Which scheme aims to provide affordable banking services to the unbanked population of India?
questions.explanation: PMJDY (Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana) aims to ensure financial inclusion by providing banking services to unbanked households.

questions.question: What is the Repo Rate used for?
options: Rate at which RBI lends to banks
Rate at which banks lend to each other
Rate at which RBI borrows from banks
Rate at which customers borrow from banks
questions.explanation: Repo Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends money to commercial banks.

questions.question: The RBI was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.question: What is the base year for the current GDP calculation in India?
questions.explanation: India revised its GDP base year from 2004-05 to 2011-12 in January 2015.

questions.question: NABARD stands for:
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
National Bureau of Agriculture and Rural Development
National Bank for Agricultural Reform and Development
New Agriculture Banking and Rural Development
questions.explanation: NABARD stands for National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, established in 1982.

questions.question: The concept of 'Financial Inclusion' in India was formally adopted following recommendations of which committee?
questions.explanation: The C. Rangarajan Committee on Financial Inclusion (2008) gave formal shape to financial inclusion policy in India.

questions.question: What is UPI in banking context?
questions.explanation: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface — a real-time payment system developed by NPCI.

questions.question: Which organization regulates the insurance sector in India?
questions.explanation: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) regulates the insurance sector in India.

questions.question: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) is an initiative by:
questions.explanation: IMPS is managed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India).

questions.question: Under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, 'Kishor' category covers loans up to:
questions.explanation: PMMY has three categories: Shishu (up to Rs.50,000), Kishor (Rs.50,001-5 lakh), Tarun (Rs.5-10 lakh).

questions.question: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a savings scheme for:
questions.explanation: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is a government savings scheme launched for the girl child under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' campaign.

questions.question: The World Bank's headquarters is located in:
questions.explanation: The World Bank Group is headquartered in Washington D.C., USA.

questions.question: IMF stands for:
questions.explanation: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund, an international organization headquartered in Washington D.C.

questions.question: India's first Digital Bank was launched in which state?
questions.explanation: India Post Payments Bank launched India's first digital bank with Airtel in Kerala.

questions.question: Which is the regulatory authority for capital markets in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the regulatory body for capital markets in India.
